The dominant problem is model serving, not React: inference takes 23–25 seconds and permits only one active request. The UI can nevertheless feel much faster before inference itself is accelerated.

| Priority | Improvement | Expected effect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Show deterministic torque measurements immediately, while OpenTSLM continues | Useful feedback in under 100 ms instead of a generic “Reading…” state |
| 2 | Display live phases and elapsed time from existing SSE tool events | Makes the 25-second wait understandable |
| 3 | Report `busy`, queue position, and estimated wait; return `Retry-After` with 409 | Prevents requests appearing broken when the single slot is occupied |
| 4 | Cache identical historical requests by checkpoint + input hash + question intent | Repeat analyses of fixed recordings become nearly instant |
| 5 | Move inference to a dedicated GPU or separate model worker process | Largest reduction in actual latency; also keeps health/data endpoints responsive |
| 6 | Stream generated tokens and stop once valid structured output is complete | Improves time-to-first-answer and potentially total generation time |
| 7 | Compress and cache replay/robot payloads | Speeds recording switches and 3D startup |
| 8 | Isolate replay rendering from the investigation panel | Removes playback jank unrelated to API latency |

- OpenTSLM generation: approximately 23–25 seconds.
- Concurrent request: `409 MODEL_BUSY`.
- `/api/health`: 145 ms idle, but observed taking 11 seconds during inference.
- Recording replay response: 4.86 MB and 1.82 seconds.
